target_customer: Hospitals and surgeons performing pelvic, urologic and colorectal surgery
problem: Surgeons risk injuring ureters and other hidden structures during surgery and lack a way to identify them in real time with their existing instruments.
business_model: Single-use medical device sold to hospitals (StimSite), FDA 510(k) pathway
product_category: Surgical medical device, electrical stimulation for ureter identification

founders.name: Albert Huang
founders.background_notes: YC page says the company was founded and run by the surgeon who created the technology. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources. Press says he became chief medical officer at Northgate after the acquisition.

technical_complexity.rationale: A hand-held stimulation device that works through existing surgical instruments needed medical device engineering and FDA clearance, which came as 510(k) K200886 in November 2020.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearance and a Safer Technologies Program designation, plus a STIMSITE trademark filed in 2020, slowed copying, but the idea of ureter identification already had lighted stent alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stryker sells lighted ureteral stent kits as an alternative, but no incumbent copied the stimulation approach found in sources; a small device maker, Northgate, bought the company in April 2023.

market_need_then: Ureter injury during pelvic surgery is a known surgical risk and lighted stents were the established but invasive identification method; the company cited a 600M dollar initial market on its YC page.

branding.domain_note: allotropemed.com, a name plus med suffix; the old site now returns 404.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and technical in YC description.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the company sold to surgeons through clinical credibility, not brand.

outcome_analysis: Allotrope was a surgeon-founded device company that raised a 4M dollar Series A in 2021 after FDA clearance of StimSite in November 2020. It reported over 5M dollars in total venture funding and was sold to Northgate Technologies in April 2023 for an undisclosed price, which fits a regulatory moat outcome but gives no evidence of large commercial scale.
notes: Company website returned 404 when fetched. Series A confirmed by a press release and VCA Online. A 2017 seed led by Houston Health Ventures and a 150K Texas Halo Fund investment appear only in aggregator or headline snippets and are unverified, so not recorded as rounds. Press says over 5M raised in total; aggregators range 4.0M to 5.3M. Competitors dated near the 2018 batch were not found, only lighted stent products with undated pages.
